decisive_step: Die-cutting and slitting jumbo rolls of self-adhesive paper (heading 4811) into individual label sheets (heading 4821) in Peru
flip: Importing the self-adhesive paper in rolls without die-cutting into individual labels in Peru, keeping the good in heading 4811 at a width over 15 cm, would leave origin in China.
reasoning: The 40-inch wide rolls of self-adhesive paper from China are classified under heading 4811 (subheading 4811.41). In Peru, the rolls are slit to letter width, die-cut into labels, printed with branding/SKU information on the liner/sheet, and cut into sheets, becoming paper labels classified under heading 4821 (4821.10 or 4821.90). Under 19 CFR 102.20, heading 4821 requires a change from any other heading. Because the Chinese paper shifts from 4811 to 4821 in Peru, 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) confers Peru origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 8422.30 from parts of 8422.90 and other headings
decisive_step: Fabrication of machine frames, machining of components, and final assembly and system integration of all subassemblies into the complete inline labeling system in Canada
flip: If the U.S.-made AE-916 MK2 labeling heads were classified as complete labeling machines under 8422.30 upon importation into Canada rather than parts under 8422.90, failing the 102.20 tariff shift and shifting origin to the United States under 102.11(b).
reasoning: The XP-200T inline labeling system is a functional unit classified under subheading 8422.30, HTSUS (machinery for labeling bottles or other containers). Under 19 CFR 102.20(o), the rule for 8422.11-8422.40 requires a change to subheading 8422.30 from any other subheading, including parts in 8422.90. All foreign components—including the U.S. labeling head subassemblies (parts of 8422.90), conveyors, motors, and sensors—undergo the required tariff shift when fabricated, assembled, and integrated into the complete system in Canada under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) (consistent with H324660 and N366064).
